title: Compounding of offences - which cases can genuinely be settled
p1:
Not every criminal case has to end with a long courtroom battle.

But can every offence simply be settled by an agreement between the parties? The answer surprises many people.
p2:
A common misconception is that if the victim and accused decide to compromise, the case automatically disappears. That is not true. The law allows only certain offences to be compounded, meaning legally settled by the affected parties.

Minor disputes like some personal conflicts, certain property-related matters, and less serious offences may qualify. Serious crimes usually cannot be privately settled because they affect society as a whole.
p3:
The key idea is this: compounding is not about who wants to forgive whom; it is about whether the law considers the offence suitable for settlement.

A practical takeaway: before spending years fighting a case, check whether the offence is legally compoundable. A settlement may save time, but only when the law permits it.
conclusion: Do you think more minor criminal disputes should be allowed to settle outside courts, or should the law keep strict limits? Share your view.
